causal_mechanism: Long-lived completion channels capture authentication metadata at channel construction; token rotation updates the token manager but leaves active channel metadata stale, causing post-rotation completion RPCs to be rejected.

causal_roles.description: Completion channel/interceptor snapshots token state instead of resolving current credentials for each RPC.
Service token rotates while a completion channel remains active.
A channel created before rotation survives and is reused afterward.
Authentication rejection is not retried through freshly authenticated metadata/channel.
Scheduler lease can expire before artifact reconciliation repairs scheduler state.
Completed job is shown as TIMED_OUT because scheduler never receives the completion transition.

causal_chain: Token manager rotates to a new valid service credential.
An already-active completion channel retains authentication metadata captured before rotation.
A completed job publishes its completion event through that stale channel.
Completion gateway rejects the RPC authentication.
Artifact and billing side effects remain committed because they occurred before completion publishing.
Scheduler receives no normal completion transition.
The job lease expires before or without reconciliation.
The job is reported as TIMED_OUT despite successful work.
accepted_reproduction: Keep a completion channel alive across forced token rotation, then show that post-rotation completion publish fails while a newly created channel succeeds.
Equivalent instrumentation proving that failed completion requests carry credential state older than TokenManager.current_token.
accepted_interventions: Resolve current token per completion RPC rather than snapshotting at channel construction.
Atomically invalidate/rebuild active completion channels when token rotation occurs, preserving concurrency safety and idempotency.
Retry authentication-rejected completion once through guaranteed-fresh credentials if all security/idempotency invariants remain satisfied.
counterfactual_variants: CF-1 rotation jitter and randomized IDs.
CF-2 reconciliation delayed beyond lease timeout.
CF-3 altered concurrency/channel-pool size with a live pre-rotation channel.

provenance.contamination_risk: high for exact public case; hidden descendants must be transformed

known_shortcuts: Increasing scheduler timeout can reduce visible incidents but does not repair completion authentication.
Restarting workers rebuilds channels and temporarily suppresses the symptom.
Blanket retry can mask delivery failure while introducing duplicate/resource risks.

causal_claim_units.claim: Long-lived completion channel/interceptor snapshots credential state at construction.
Token rotation updates the token manager without updating already-active channel authentication metadata.
A post-rotation completion RPC can fail authentication after artifact and billing side effects have already committed.
Missing completion transition leads to scheduler lease expiry and the timeout manifestation.
Restart or channel recreation temporarily restores correct authentication state.
